workflow: Open Quick Editing below Home or use the top shortcut.
Select the file and start automatic execution.

controls: Past executions: load the first page of saved rules.
Condition / Formula rules: choose the expression family and filter by discovery method.
Previous / Next: fetch only the selected page from the server.

Violation details: load stored violation rows for the selected rule. Filter by condition count and exclude zero counts. Rules with violations come first by count, followed by unrecorded and zero counts; this is not an error-probability ranking. Back to rules restores filters, page and position. Detected totals can differ from saved previews, and 70% confidence alone does not establish whether preview rows exist.
Statistics, column types and diagnostics: load each result on demand.
Detailed results: open Rule Discovery Analysis in the main workspace.
Reset: clear screen progress while retaining saved server results.
aiGuidance: Continuous columns do not guarantee a valid formula.

The detail layer remains independently scrollable in expanded view and at high browser zoom.

Look up the user, role, and access scope in the system DB.
Resolve the current Target DB connection on the server.
Dispatch to the menu router and shared service.
outputs: Service call using the Target DB connection
checks: New APIs require login by default.
Menu hiding is a UI aid; the server role check is the security boundary.

target-context.title: Project, scenario, and Target DB
target-context.summary: Bind project scope, execution scenario, and managed target table into one work context.

callFlow: Select a project and scenario.
Upload a file or browse a Target DB table.
Save the scenario target table.
Optionally provision the four default Jobs and Flow.
checks: Verify the intended Target DB before execution.
Keep the source baseline and editable copy separate.

orchestrator.title: Flow design, validation, and execution
orchestrator.summary: Connect saved Jobs as a DAG and validate artifacts, order, cycles, and SAME_RUN dependencies.

detail.overview: A Flow is an executable DAG. The current executor processes the validated topological order and records every node state and output under one Flow Run.
callFlow: Place Jobs saved in M03001–M03004 on the canvas.
Define prerequisite and completion edges.
Validate cycles, reverse stages, ports, artifacts, and required SAME_RUN inputs.
Start Run now or Queue batch.
Record SUCCESS, FAILED, or SKIPPED for each node; partial subtask completion is persisted as FAILED with a review message.
inputs: Job definitions and actual runtime parameters
checks: A successful Validate proves structure and contracts, not data-processing success.
Solid edges require upstream SUCCESS; ON_COMPLETE edges require a terminal state.
The current default executor is ordered, not parallel.

job-contract.title: Saved Job, runtime binds, and result contract
job-contract.summary: Resolve target, result, upstream input, and Run IDs, then route to DB, OML Python, or API execution.

detail.overview: Each node references a saved data Job. The server merges Job defaults with Flow edges and system values before selecting the execution adapter.
callFlow: Load the Job and execution resource specification.
Merge saved values, reserved runtime values, and upstream output.
Validate identifiers, required values, and SAME_RUN contracts.
Dispatch WEB_API to the API executor, and DB_OBJECT or OML_PYTHON to the saved-script execution path.
Normalize output into artifacts and the Node Run message.
inputs: Flow Run ID and upstream output
checks: Actual saved parameters for the selected Run override preset examples.
Identifiers and dynamic fragments are allow-listed before execution.

internal-model.title: Internal model and Target DB object
internal-model.summary: Run registered procedures, packages, and Oracle ML models through the server Target DB connection.
internal-model.artifact: PL/SQL / ORACLE ML → TABLE or MODEL

detail.overview: Internal models are Target DB objects registered in M90001. New unified stages call INTERNAL_API functions that reuse existing Oracle analysis, including categorical Apriori. Previously saved DB_OBJECT Jobs continue to use their registered execution route.
callFlow: Read registered object and parameter metadata.
Prepare the session Target DB connection and runtime binds.
Execute the saved PL/SQL block with binds.
Associate table or model output with the same Run.
Record DB output and execution state.
outputs: Column, relation, rule, or violation tables
Oracle ML model and execution message
checks: Object names and parameters must match the Target DB definition.
Review parallel resources, scope limits, and commit units for large analysis jobs.

oml-python.title: OML Python route
oml-python.summary: Invoke OML4Py SQL APIs and Script Repository resources according to the registered execution method.

detail.overview: OML Python is an optional Target DB OML4Py resource path. The registered method and parameter contract determine the SQL API and normalized result shape.
callFlow: Load the OML Python resource and execution method.
Bind target data and runtime parameters.
Execute the registered script through the selected OML4Py SQL API.
Map the response to a table or model artifact.
checks: The execution method and return shape must match the resource contract.
Check Target DB privileges, OML4Py installation, and ACL configuration.

api-resource.title: Internal Python API and external JSON API
api-resource.summary: All four new unified stages call same-server functions directly; only external API extensions make remote HTTP calls.

detail.overview: M90002 is an API Object Registry. New default Jobs use UNIFIED_EDITING_PROFILE/RELATION/DISCOVER/DETECT through WEB_API and the direct INTERNAL_API adapter. Each function runs existing Oracle analysis followed by mixed Python analysis. Unregistered built-in Jobs use their saved contracts; only EXTERNAL_API makes remote HTTP calls.
callFlow: Read API type, method, endpoint, and I/O contract.
Build the payload from Target, Run, and upstream artifacts.
Call INTERNAL_API as a direct server function without HTTP loopback.
For EXTERNAL_API, send a GET query or JSON body to an absolute http(s) endpoint.
Validate timeout, response size, and JSON, then apply the output contract.
inputs: Registered API spec and actual Run parameters
Latest finalized types for stage 2 (LATEST_MASTER) and SAME_RUN upstream artifacts for stages 3–4
Credentials entered in the runtime-bind dialog for EXTERNAL_API
outputs: Relation network, LASSO, Symbolic rule, and violation results
Mapped table, model, or JSON output from a user API
checks: Do not describe the default INTERNAL_API as an internet model call.
External responses must be valid JSON within configured limits.
EXTERNAL_API credentials are included in browser memory and the execution request; this path does not resolve them automatically from a server-side secret store.

stage-1.title: Column type analysis
stage-1.summary: UNIFIED_EDITING_PROFILE supplements existing column-type classification with sampled statistics, numeric-text and data-quality diagnostics.

detail.overview: Unified PROFILE retains INIT$_SP_PREDICTED_TYPE classification and confirmed labels, then adds bounded-sample statistics and numeric-text/invalid-value diagnostics. Supplementary diagnostics do not overwrite source types or finalized labels. The classification details below describe the existing Oracle sub-analysis.
callFlow: Resolve target table and execution parameters.
Profile type, nullness, distinctness, length, numeric ratio, entropy, and distribution.
Combine base rules with active OML predictions.
Persist per-Run and final column types separately.
algorithm: Use deterministic sampling for stable large-table profiles.
Combine rule results with model confidence.
Keep rule output when the model returns no usable prediction.
inputs: Active column-type model for the Target DB
checks: A numeric data type alone does not prove continuous business meaning.
Distinguish Run types from current final types.
Actual Run thresholds override presets.

stage-2.title: Column relation analysis
stage-2.summary: UNIFIED_EDITING_RELATION adds mixed numeric/categorical, missing-value and duplicate diagnostics to the existing matrix and network.

detail.overview: Unified RELATION keeps the type-aware matrix, network and clusters, then separately samples Pearson, bias-corrected Cramér's V, correlation ratio eta, missingness and duplicates. Existing pass thresholds and supplementary sample metrics remain distinct. The network details below describe the existing sub-analysis.
callFlow: Read final column types and target data.
Compute the type-specific metric and, where supported, its significance probability.
Apply actual thresholds and store PASS status.
Select strong edges and create deterministic weighted communities.
algorithm: Categorical × categorical: Cramér's V and p-value
Continuous × continuous: Pearson and optional Spearman
Weighted community, degree, and centrality from passing edges
inputs: Significance, strength, sample, and edge limits
checks: Passing correlation is not causation or a final business rule.
Below-threshold variables may still matter in multivariate formulas.
Clusters are optional guidance for discovery.

stage-3.title: Automatic rule discovery
stage-3.summary: UNIFIED_EDITING_DISCOVER saves existing Apriori/LASSO/Symbolic results and mixed value, range and formula candidates in the same run.

detail.overview: Unified DISCOVER runs existing Apriori and LASSO/Symbolic analysis, then discovers actual-value/range trees and mixed formulas. Model and source identities remain separate. A mixed success does not hide a failed existing analysis. The P_RULE_PARTS and cluster options below apply to the existing branch; inspect separate P_MIXED_* settings for supplementary analysis.
callFlow: Choose categorical and/or continuous parts.
Build an Apriori model and readable categorical-rule summaries.
Use LASSO to select continuous features.
Search symbolic or polynomial formulas and evaluate stability.
Persist candidates with quality metrics.
algorithm: Apriori applies support, confidence, length, and combination budgets.
LASSO uses median imputation, scaling, and sparse coefficient selection.
Symbolic search compares linear, robust, ratio, polynomial-LASSO, and optional PySR candidates.
Non-NONE cluster mode consumes the same Run's RELATION_NETWORK.
inputs: Part, threshold, candidate, budget, and time limits
checks: Discovered rules are candidates, not approvals.
LASSO features and accepted formulas are different results.
Interpret quality metrics and business meaning together.

stage-4.title: Rule violation detection
stage-4.summary: UNIFIED_EDITING_DETECT applies same-run existing and mixed rules and preserves each source's violation candidates.

detail.overview: Unified DETECT applies existing association/Symbolic rules and mixed value/range/formula ASTs within the same run. Mismatches, missing outcomes and tolerance violations are review candidates, not automatic source edits. Rule-row counts may overlap across analyses and must not be summed as unique erroneous rows or cells.
callFlow: Verify selected parts and same-Run rule artifacts.
Validate categorical conditions or safe symbolic expressions.
Compare actual rows with expected or predicted values.
Persist violations within per-rule limits.
Record subtask and overall node states.
algorithm: Categorical: condition match plus null or mismatched result.
Continuous: allowed formula and feature evaluation with relative and absolute error thresholds.
Per-part savepoints can preserve one successful part if the other fails.
inputs: Same-Run association model and rule summary
Tolerance, rule, scan, and storage limits
outputs: Continuous actual, predicted, and error details
checks: SUCCESS with zero violations can be a valid outcome.
When a Node is FAILED, use its partial-completion message to separate successful and failed parts.
Corrections occur later in M05002.

run-artifacts.title: Run and node-result artifacts
run-artifacts.summary: Bind stage results, actual parameters, states, and messages into a traceable Flow Run.

detail.overview: Every node input, output, and state belongs to a Flow Run. SAME_RUN validation checks whether an upstream node in that Run declares the required artifact contract, while analysis reads both stored history and actual results.
callFlow: Issue Flow Run and Node Run IDs.
Record start, finish, failure, and skip states.
Attach actual runtime parameters and result targets.
Expose messages and artifacts to analysis.
inputs: Node result and standard output contract
outputs: Basis for Result SQL and model details
checks: Distinguish stored SUCCESS, FAILED, and SKIPPED states, and review partial-completion messages on FAILED nodes.
Single-node runs still need required upstream SAME_RUN inputs.

analysis.title: Integrated discovery analysis
analysis.summary: Visualize the four-stage Run as column types, relation clusters, rules, and violations.

detail.overview: M04002 presents each model result using a type-aware table, chart, network, or rule view and separates execution status from result quality.
callFlow: Find the Flow Run by project, scenario, and state.
Load node states and artifacts.
Render the appropriate result view.
Export selected data or continue to rule decisions.
inputs: Model, relation, rule, violation, and sample results
checks: Execution success is not business approval.
Review samples with totals and actual thresholds.

editing.title: Rule decision, correction, and production application
editing.summary: Finalize candidates, correct an editable copy, validate effects, then confirm and execute versioned production DML.

detail.overview: Discovery results never apply directly to source data. Rule decisions, editable-copy changes, effect validation, and DML generation, validation, saving, and execution remain separate and auditable.
callFlow: Select or exclude candidates and validate user rules in M05001.
Prepare the editable work table and correct violation cells in M05002.
Validate before-and-after effects and optionally rerun the Flow in M05003.
Server-revalidate saved DML, then confirm and execute it for an editing session whose effects have been validated.
Record all major events in audit history.
checks: Rule decisions, editable-copy effect validation, and production DML execution are separate steps.
Completed DML is versioned rather than overwritten.

reports.title: Basic and custom reports
reports.summary: Package projects, Runs, rules, and editing history into fixed or user-designed reports.

detail.overview: Basic Reports provide a fixed catalog and integrated report; Custom Reports arrange reusable blocks in a saved user template.
callFlow: Select project, scenario, and baseline Run.
Check available analysis and editing results.
Preview an individual, integrated, or custom report.
Generate M06001 reports as HTML, Excel (XLSX), or PDF, and M06002 custom reports as HTML or PDF.
inputs: Decision, correction, validation, and application history
checks: Show the baseline project, scenario, and Run.
Do not include projects outside the user's access scope.

M03001.title: Column Type Analysis
M03001.label: Column Type Analysis
M03001.summary: Review or tune the automatically created UNIFIED_EDITING_PROFILE Job, or configure individual models. It combines existing type classification with sampled statistics and numeric-text diagnostics while preserving finalized labels.
purpose: Create the shared column-type contract for correlation, rule discovery, and violation detection.
Review statistics, missing values, distinct counts, and the reason for each classification.

layout.name: Run-based Column Type
layout.description: The default tab. Shows the classification produced by the selected run.

layout.name: Final Column Type
layout.description: Shows the finalized type that downstream jobs may reuse.

layout.description: Shows the actual saved parameters and result contract for the job.

workflow: Select the scenario and target table.

Open the automatically created Job to restore its saved model and parameters, or choose a model for a new Job. An unregistered built-in Job restores its saved contract without requiring central registration.
Import creates a new draft with the source contract and parameters. Review the target, generate the execution-type-specific PL/SQL, OML SQL or API spec, then save.

M03002.title: Column Correlation Analysis
M03002.label: Column Correlation Analysis
M03002.summary: Review or tune the automatically created UNIFIED_EDITING_RELATION Job, or configure individual models. It combines the existing relationship matrix, network and clusters with sampled mixed relationships, missingness and duplicate diagnostics.
purpose: Compare all pair types with the metric appropriate to each data-type combination.
Separate passed and below-threshold pairs while retaining both in the integrated matrix.
Summarize strong relationships as network edges, nodes, and clusters.

layout.name: Integrated Relationship Matrix
layout.description: The default tab. Filters all, passed, or below-threshold pairs and updates pair-type counts together.

layout.name: Categorical Correlation
layout.description: Shows passed categorical-categorical pairs.

layout.name: Continuous Correlation
layout.description: Shows passed continuous-continuous pairs.

layout.name: Relationship Network
layout.description: Combines edge details with node and cluster summaries in one view.

deepDive: PASS_YN distinguishes pairs that passed the actual run thresholds from pairs retained for review.
Clusters are optional guidance for rule discovery and are applied only when P_CLUSTER_USAGE_MODE enables them.
workflow: Open the saved UNIFIED_EDITING_RELATION Job and its parameters, or choose a model for a new Job. Keep existing-analysis and mixed-analysis options distinct.
Import creates a new draft. Review its target and source contract, generate the API spec for a unified Web API, then save.
Save and run the job, then review the integrated matrix, pair-type tabs, and relationship network.
controls: Save Job / Run, Run History, result-tab filters, network controls, grid tools, and export.
aiGuidance: Use the selected Run ID, PASS_YN, pair type, actual thresholds, and cluster method when interpreting results.
The network requires edge data; cluster metadata changes grouping but is not required merely to draw edges.

M03003.title: Automatic Rule Discovery
M03003.label: Automatic Rule Discovery
M03003.summary: Review or tune the automatically created UNIFIED_EDITING_DISCOVER Job. It supplements existing Apriori/LASSO/Symbolic results with mixed actual-value, range and formula rules; individual models remain available.
purpose: Discover categorical IF/THEN association rules.
Select important continuous features and generate f(x)=y symbolic rules.
Optionally prefer or restrict candidates by relationship-network cluster.

layout.name: Categorical Automatic Rules
layout.description: Combines the association model and stored rule summary into one readable rule view.

layout.name: Continuous Automatic Rules
layout.description: Compares LASSO feature importance with generated symbolic formulas and target status.

deepDive: P_RULE_PARTS selects ALL, CATEGORICAL, or CONTINUOUS work in the existing analysis branch. Supplementary mixed analysis has separate settings.
P_CLUSTER_USAGE_MODE supports NONE, PREFER_SAME_CLUSTER, and WITHIN_CLUSTER_ONLY. PREFER_SAME_CLUSTER is the safer default because cross-cluster predictors can remain eligible.
When cluster usage is enabled, a RELATION_NETWORK result from the same run is required.
An important LASSO feature may be absent from symbolic formulas because of R-squared, auto-target range, or feature-selection limits.
troubleshooting: If only categorical results appear, check P_RULE_PARTS, continuous target eligibility, minimum R-squared, auto-target limits, and partial-completion messages.
workflow: Open the saved UNIFIED_EDITING_DISCOVER Job and its parameters, or choose an individual model. Built-in Jobs without a registry ID retain their saved contract.
Import creates a new draft with source parameters and contract. Review the target and upstream input, generate the execution-type-specific script or API spec, then save.
Save and run the Job, then inspect paged condition and formula rules in M04002. Each rule retains its discovery method. Distinguish confidence/lift from tolerance coverage and validation R-squared.
controls: Save Job / Run, Run History, rule-type tabs, detail and graph layers, grid tools, and export.
aiGuidance: Show column labels with IDs and distinguish an association-rule result from a symbolic prediction target.
Explain target counts from the saved run parameters, not only from preset defaults.

M03004.title: Rule Violation Detection
M03004.label: Rule Violation Detection
M03004.summary: Review or tune the automatically created UNIFIED_EDITING_DETECT Job. It applies same-run existing association/Symbolic rules and mixed value/range/formula rules, keeping violation rows scoped by source.
purpose: Detect records that contradict categorical condition/result rules.
Detect continuous values outside the configured absolute or percentage error tolerance.

layout.name: Categorical Rule Violations
layout.description: Shows candidate, exception, and violating-row counts for association rules.

layout.name: Continuous Rule Violations
layout.description: Shows predicted/actual values, error measures, and violating rows for symbolic rules.

deepDive: P_RULE_PARTS selects ALL, CATEGORICAL, or CONTINUOUS detection in the existing analysis branch. Supplementary mixed detection uses the same run's mixed rules.
P_SYMBOLIC_RULE_TABLE_NAME refers to the symbolic rule storage table, not an association-model name or arbitrary previous result table.
P_RULE_ID=(auto) evaluates all eligible symbolic rules; a specific ID evaluates only that rule.
With P_CONTINUE_ON_ERROR=Y, one subtask may succeed while another fails, so review partial-completion details.
troubleshooting: A successful result with zero rows can mean no violation exceeded the current thresholds; distinguish it from missing rule inputs or a failed subtask.
workflow: Open the saved UNIFIED_EDITING_DETECT Job and its parameters, or select an individual detection model. A built-in Job does not require a central registry ID.
Import creates a new draft. Review the target, same-run rule input and source contract, generate the API spec for a unified Web API, then save.
Save and run the Job, then select a condition or formula rule to load its saved violation rows. Preserve each method's metric meanings; overlapping rule-row counts are not unique error counts.
controls: Save Job / Run, Run History, rule-part tabs, violation-row detail, grid tools, and export.
aiGuidance: Distinguish association IF/THEN violations from symbolic predicted/actual error violations.
Report partial success and failed subtasks separately when continue-on-error is enabled.

M04001.title: Rule Discovery Execution
M04001.label: Rule Discovery Execution
M04001.summary: Designs, validates, and runs a reusable four-stage DAG from saved data jobs, with artifact compatibility and same-run dependencies enforced at connection time.
purpose: Connect column typing, relationship analysis, rule discovery, and violation detection as one flow.
Use four integrated jobs for the standard path while retaining individual categorical, continuous, LASSO, Apriori, symbolic, and other jobs when needed.

layout.name: Flow Designer
layout.description: Shows representative IN/OUT ports, T for table artifacts, M for model artifacts, and stage-specific connector shapes.

layout.name: Node Inspector
layout.description: Shows the selected node's actual runtime binds, upstream dependency, and result contract.

layout.name: Input and Output Contracts
layout.description: Explains artifact compatibility, REQUIRED/OPTIONAL inputs, SAME_RUN, and solid/dashed execution conditions.

deepDive: Square, triangle, circle, and diamond ports represent stages 1 through 4 respectively.
REQUIRED plus SAME_RUN means the downstream node must receive the compatible result produced earlier in the same flow run.
If P_CLUSTER_USAGE_MODE is not NONE, integrated rule discovery requires the same run's RELATION_NETWORK result.
Port shape compatibility and solid/dashed execution conditions are separate checks and both must pass validation.
troubleshooting: For a rejected connection, compare the output and input artifact names, stage shapes, REQUIRED/OPTIONAL setting, and SAME_RUN policy.
workflow: Select a project, scenario, and saved Flow or create a new one.
Save imported drafts in M03001-M03004 before adding them. Verify each node's saved Job, target and stage contract, connect compatible ports, validate and save the DAG, then execute it.
Use Run History for status, node results, retry, and automatic refresh.
controls: Flow Design, Run History, Result SQL, Save Flow, Validate, Run, Refresh, Retry, and node parameter detail.
aiGuidance: Delete Node removes the node from the current draft canvas; it does not directly delete saved jobs or run history.
In editing revalidation mode, saved Flow definitions stay unchanged and only runtime target owner/table parameters are overridden with INITDN$.

M04002.title: Rule Discovery Analysis
M04002.label: Rule Discovery Analysis
M04002.summary: Analyzes a selected flow run through stage-specific integrated result tabs for column types, relationships and clusters, automatic rules, and rule violations.

layout.name: Scenario Runs
layout.description: Selecting a run resets prior node/tab state and builds results for that run.

layout.name: Integrated Results
layout.description: Loads a tab on first use, reuses it within the same run, and preserves vertical scroll while switching tabs.

layout.name: Stage Results
layout.description: Preserves early profiling and relationship diagnostics. Final condition and formula rules load 20 at a time; select a rule for saved violations or its original source analysis.

deepDive: The integrated relationship matrix includes PASS_YN=Y and N and supports All, Passed, and Below threshold filters.
The relationship network combines edge and node/cluster information in one screen.
LASSO features are candidates; symbolic formulas are generated rules. The target status is derived from the selected run's actual parameters.
A successful violation task with zero rows is not automatically an error. Check rule counts, thresholds, and partial-completion messages.

Mixed summary metrics, detail grids, and CSV exports follow the selected rule type. Formula within-tolerance rates and validation R-squared are distinct from value-rule confidence and lift. Counts from overlapping analysis sources are not unique error-row counts.
troubleshooting: If one categorical or continuous section is missing, check P_RULE_PARTS, upstream same-run inputs, and failed-subtask details.
purpose: Interpret a selected Flow Run without redesigning or rerunning the Flow.
Compare integrated stage results and open model, rule, graph, and violating-row details.
workflow: Select a project, scenario, and Run.

Open stage or node tabs. For discovery and detection, select condition or formula rules and optionally filter by discovery method. Historical anomaly explanations remain separate from actual-value rules.
Use Review Editing Rules to continue with rule decisions when appropriate.
controls: Filter by condition count and exclude zero counts. Rules with violations come first by count, followed by unrecorded and zero counts; this is not an error-probability ranking. Back to rules restores filters, page and position. Detected totals can differ from saved previews, and 70% confidence alone does not establish whether preview rows exist.
Run selection, stage/node tabs, result filters, detail/graph layers, grid tools, export, and Review Editing Rules.
aiGuidance: Always state the selected Run ID and distinguish baseline runs from INITDN$ editing-revalidation runs.
Result SQL generated from a result table should include available Run ID, table, model, and source conditions but not placeholder literals as data filters.

M05001.title: Editing Rule Management
M05001.label: Rule Decision & Master
M05001.summary: Uses one shared project/scenario scope for a Rule Decision tab that contains discovered results only and a Rule Master tab that manages final selected and user-defined rules.
purpose: Review categorical association rules and continuous symbolic rules from a Flow Run, then select or exclude them.
Validate, create, update, copy, or delete user-defined rules separately from discovered rules.

layout.name: Project / Scenario
layout.description: The collapsible work scope shared by both tabs.

layout.name: Rule Decision
layout.description: Uses server paging and Run source, Run ID, rule type, decision status, and violation-presence filters for discovered rules.

layout.name: Rule Master
layout.description: Separates selected discovered rules from user rules and provides the user-rule editor below the fixed-height grid.

layout.name: Rule Detail Layer
layout.description: Shows IF/THEN or f(x) details plus live violation count, rows, and SQL from the current full INITUP$ table.

workflow: Select a project and scenario, then load the latest Run automatically or enter a Run ID.
The default Error Rules Only filter returns rules that have stored violation-detection rows for the selected Run; switch to All or Normal Rules Only when needed.
Use Realtime to inspect actual violations in the current full INITUP$ table before selecting a rule.
Filter and inspect rule details, then select or exclude checked candidates; bulk selection validates every selected rule live first.
Open Rule Master to review final rules or validate a user-defined association or formula rule against the current full table before saving it.
controls: Search: applies Run, rule, decision, and violation-presence filters through the server query.
Realtime: runs server-generated read-only SQL against the current full INITUP$ table and shows actual violation rows.
Select / Exclude: validates selected rules live before selection and processes checked discovered rules with an inline progress bar.
User Rule: validates live and creates, updates, copies, or deletes a user-origin rule.
Exclude Selection: excludes checked discovered-origin master rules.
Grid tools: search, refresh, server paging, freeze columns, and export.
aiGuidance: The Rule Decision tab contains discovered results only; user rules are stored and shown only in Rule Master.
Even when All Scenarios is selected, a selected rule is stored with the project and scenario IDs carried by that result row.
Do not describe association IF/THEN rules and continuous f(x)/prediction targets as the same rule format.
A discovered rule is copied to a user rule before editing; it is excluded rather than physically deleted.

M05002.title: Editing Error Correction
M05002.label: Editing Error Correction
M05002.summary: Checks live INITUP$ data with final selected and active rules, edits values only in its one-to-one INITDN$ copy, and keeps correction history in a second cached tab.
purpose: Run live violation SQL generated from final Rule Master rules against the selected INITUP$ table.
Preserve INITUP$ while saving single or multiple corrected values into INITDN$.

layout.name: Editing Work Tables
layout.description: Shows Rule Master INITUP$ tables and their matching INITDN$ tables as a single-select grid.

layout.name: Error Correction
layout.description: Filters live violations by rule type, error column, correction status, and final rule, then edits them in the same grid.

layout.name: Correction History
layout.description: Shows row key, column, before/after values, rule, operator, and edit time for the selected table mapping.

workflow: Select one INITUP$/INITDN$ mapping row.
If INITDN$ does not exist, create the one-to-one editing table from that row.
Run the live violation query and save one row or checked rows into INITDN$.
Use Correction History to review or export the stored cell-edit events.
controls: Create Editing Table: prepares and selects the INITDN$ copy.
Search / Live SQL: executes the live query or displays its read-only SQL.
Save Selected Corrections / Save Correction: validates and stores values in INITDN$.
Rule Detail: combines the M05001 rule detail with the selected violation result.
Grid tools: search, refresh, server paging, freeze columns, and export.
aiGuidance: INITUP$ is never edited by this screen; all corrections are written to INITDN$.
Search executes live SQL against the current table, while Live SQL only displays that statement.
Before INITDN$ exists, the result grid is read-only and edit controls are hidden.
Rows without a business key are linked through the stored INIT$_SOURCE_ROWID value.

M05003.title: Editing Production Deployment
M05003.label: Editing Production Deployment
M05003.summary: Validates editing effects, manages versioned production DML, and reviews the complete editing audit trail in three cached tabs.
purpose: Compare INITUP$ baseline analysis with the linked INITDN$ rule-discovery rerun.
Generate, validate, save, and execute a guarded PL/SQL apply block.
Trace events from rule decisions through final operational apply.

layout.name: Effect Validation
layout.description: Loads a fast stored summary first and runs the full INITUP$/INITDN$ rule comparison only on demand.

layout.name: Production Apply
layout.description: Shows DML versions by descending DML ID and an always-editable SQL editor with the selected DML ID.

layout.name: Full History
layout.description: Filters and exports editing audit events for the selected work table.

workflow: Select one INITUP$/INITDN$ work-table row, review the fast summary, and run Detailed Effect Analysis only when a full same-rule comparison is needed.
Create a new DML or regenerate the selected version's initial SQL, then edit its name or SQL if needed.
Validate explicitly or save directly; Save validates first and writes only when valid.
Execute a validated and saved DML, then review the audit event.
controls: Detailed Effect Analysis: evaluates rules in bounded conditional-aggregation batches to reduce table scans.
Rerun Rule Discovery / Complete Effect Validation: links reanalysis and saves validation only after Detailed Effect Analysis is complete.
Create New DML: adds a visible New · Unsaved row and server-generated PL/SQL.
Regenerate Initial SQL: resets the selected version to the current editing changes.
Validate DML / Save DML / Execute DML: validate, automatically validate-and-save, or commit the final apply.
Edit / Delete: opens a version in the editor or deletes a non-executed saved DML after confirmation.
Grid tools: DML ID descending order, search, refresh, paging, freeze columns, and export.
aiGuidance: DML execution changes the operational INITUP$ source and commits, so confirm status and affected rows.
Executed DML cannot be deleted or overwritten; an edited copy is saved as a new version after confirmation.
Draft, validated/saved, and failed DML versions update the same DML ID when selected and saved.
New unsaved rows use an amber background; the selected saved row uses a stronger blue background.

M06001.label: Basic Reports

purpose: Compare different datasets with the same report types and metric definitions.
Trace the full path from rule-discovery design through decisions, corrections, validation, and production deployment.
Review an individual report or the complete fixed catalog in a separate window and download HTML, XLSX, or PDF.

layout.name: Project Cards
layout.description: A responsive, server-paged card grid shows project attributes and editing metrics.

layout.name: Report Context
layout.description: Project, scenario, Flow Run, and editing session fix the basis for every report.

layout.name: Fixed Report Catalog
layout.description: All 21 reports remain in a stable order with available, partial, no-data, or not-applicable states.

layout.name: Individual Report Window

layout.name: Combined Report Window

Select a scenario and review the automatically chosen Flow Run and editing session.
Adjust the Run or session if needed, then open a report card or select Generate Combined Report.
Review the individual or combined report window, then download the required format.
controls: Project search, load more, and back to project list.
Scenario, Flow Run, and editing session selectors.
Open an individual report, generate the combined report, and download HTML, XLSX, or PDF.
aiGuidance: Use numerator and denominator values when comparing rate metrics across different data volumes.
Only allowlisted M04001 parameters are exposed; passwords, tokens, API keys, wallets, and connection strings are excluded.
Raw DML SQL and original audit summaries or detail JSON that may contain row identifiers are excluded from Basic Reports.
On mobile, cards and context controls become a single column, and table rows become label-value cards without horizontal scrolling.

M06002.label: Custom Reports
M06002.summary: Arrange the 20 Basic Reports in a chosen paper layout, select their detail blocks, and save the result as a reusable Custom Reports template.
purpose: Select only the editing reports needed for a project's specific reporting purpose.
Save paper size, orientation, report placement, and detail-block order as a template reusable across projects.
Preview a complete document with current data and download it as HTML or PDF.

layout.name: Project Cards
layout.description: Review each project's Custom Reports count, generation count, and recent report layouts, then select a project to design.

layout.name: Report Context
layout.description: Choose the scenario, rule-discovery Run, and editing session used by the preview.

layout.name: Template and Paper

layout.name: Layout Designer

layout.name: Detail Block Editor
layout.description: Select and reorder the KPI, table, and description blocks shown for each report.

layout.name: Full Preview
layout.description: Review pages populated with live report data and download HTML or PDF.

workflow: Select a project, then confirm its scenario, Flow Run, and editing session.
Load a saved template or set the name and paper options for a new template.
Add Basic Reports from the palette and configure their layout and detail blocks.
Save or apply the template, then review and download the full preview.
controls: Project search and scenario, Flow Run, and editing-session selectors.
Create, save, delete, and apply templates.
Add, remove, reorder, and configure report detail blocks.
A4/A3, portrait/landscape, full preview, and HTML/PDF downloads.
aiGuidance: Custom Reports do not change the definitions or calculations of Basic Reports; they only select reports, blocks, and display order.
Templates belong to the signed-in user within the current Target DB and do not store project source data or execution results in layout JSON.
Template saves and applications are summarized per project on the project cards.
Preview and download requests revalidate server access to the selected project, scenario, Run, and session.
On mobile, panels and report tables become a single column or label-value cards without horizontal scrolling.

M07001.label: Editing Effect Validation

purpose: Compare the INITUP$ baseline Run with the linked INITDN$ rule-discovery rerun.
Review saved changes, expected/predicted matches, and violation changes.

layout.name: Editing Work Tables
layout.description: Selects one work table to validate.

layout.name: Validation Results
layout.description: Shows row-level results and baseline/editing Run context.

workflow: Select a work table, link a rerun, review results, and complete effect validation.
controls: Rerun Rule Discovery, Search, Complete Effect Validation, and export.

Distinguish the baseline Run from the INITDN$ reanalysis Run.

M07002.label: Production Apply

layout.name: Full History Grid

controls: Search, refresh, detail, paging, freeze columns, and export.

Answer history questions by work session, operator, time, event type, and entity ID.

M90001.title: Internal Model Registration
M90001.label: Internal Model Registration
M90001.summary: Browses Target DB procedures, packages, and model objects and registers them as executable internal resources without changing object IDs or parameter names.
purpose: Standardize descriptions, result contracts, and defaults for column typing, relationship, rule, and violation procedures.
Expose accurate parameter comments in Data Work and the Flow node inspector.
Manage INIT$_SP_PREDICTED_TYPE model defaults and Target DB-specific overrides from the model resource itself.

layout.name: Object Tree

Verify that its actual parameter names and types match the preset metadata.
For INIT$_SP_PREDICTED_TYPE, review or edit Target DB overrides in Column Type Classification Settings.
Review the result table/model contract and defaults, then register the resource.

Deleting a column-type override restores the model default; applying preset overrides may overwrite existing Target DB overrides.
P_SYMBOLIC_RULE_TABLE_NAME identifies symbolic rule storage, not an association model.

M90002.label: External Model Registration
M90002.summary: Registers built-in Python APIs, external APIs, OML4Py resources, script-repository resources, and their call contracts and default JSON.

Keep method, endpoint, parameter names, types, defaults, descriptions, and result contracts consistent.

layout.name: API Object Groups

layout.name: API Object Detail
layout.description: Shows resource type, method, endpoint, description, and invocation metadata.

Review method, endpoint, output mode, parameters, and default JSON.

When P_CLUSTER_USAGE_MODE is not NONE, the same run's relationship-network input is required.
P_CONTINUE_ON_ERROR=Y may produce a partial integrated result, so report successful and failed subtasks separately.

M90003.label: Model Training Management

Train and compare candidate models without replacing the production model automatically.
Review detailed type codes together with the final categorical, continuous, and other type groups.

layout.name: Model Family Selector
layout.description: Selects the training family and Target DB, and displays the active physical model name.

layout.name: Overview

layout.name: Training Data & Label Quality

layout.name: Train & Compare

layout.name: Model Versions / Run History

workflow: Select a model family and review its active model name and available training labels.

Review confirmed labels, duplicates, and conflicts in Training Data & Label Quality.
Configure algorithm, feature version, maximum input rows, and other bounded settings to train a candidate.
After candidate training, the same run automatically records accuracy, balanced accuracy, Macro F1, per-class metrics, group accuracy, and confusion metrics for comparison with the active model.
Activate only a validated candidate; roll back to a previous version when necessary.
Use Run History to review input counts, completion, and errors.
controls: Model family: selects the shared model family to train or compare.
Current Target DB: refreshes model status for the Target DB in the current login session.
Training data search: filters labels by status, final type group, and keywords.
Train candidate: trains a new candidate without changing the production model.
Compare / Activate: compares quality and activates a selected validated version.
Rollback / Archive: restores an earlier version or archives an unused one.

The active model name is the physical model recorded in the active-model registry. INIT$_SP_PREDICTED_TYPE reads it directly, so M03001 does not accept a model-name parameter or own a separate training job.
Column-type training uses profile features such as distinct ratio, entropy, data type, nullness, and length; it does not expose original business rows in this screen.
When quality is low or a type group lacks confirmed examples, improve label quality and sample size before training another candidate.

M99003.summary: Supports system initialization checks, system table review, user approval, password reset, and administrator operations.
purpose: Review system initialization and application-table status.
Approve, reset, or deactivate users through server-side administrator authorization.

layout.name: System Status
layout.description: Shows initialization and application-table status.

layout.name: System Tables
layout.description: Inspects permitted system-table columns and data.

layout.name: User Administration
layout.description: Manages approval, password reset, and deactivation.

workflow: Review status first, inspect the required table or user, then confirm the intended administrative action.
controls: Status, Initialize / Truncate, Approve User, Reset Password, and Deactivate.
aiGuidance: Every administrator action requires server-session role validation; hiding or showing the front-end menu is not an authorization boundary.
Treat temporary passwords as secrets and require explicit confirmation for initialization, truncation, or password-reset actions.

M99004.title: Notice Management
M99004.label: Notice Management
M99004.summary: Lets administrators create, update, delete, and attach files to notices shown on the HOME screen and related areas.
purpose: Manage notice content, type, visibility, display period, and attachments.

layout.name: Notice List
layout.description: Searches and selects notices.

layout.name: Notice Detail
layout.description: Edits title, content, type, visibility, and display period.

layout.name: Attachments
layout.description: Uploads, downloads, or deletes notice files.

workflow: Search notices, create or select one, save its display settings, then manage attachments.
controls: Search Notices, Save Notice, Upload Files, Delete Notice, and Delete File.
aiGuidance: Deleting a notice or attachment requires the selected target and confirmation.
